extracted.intended_audience: advocates, legal services staff, and community organizations submitting public comments on CMS's Medicare Part C & D proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: A template and instructions for drafting and submitting public comments on CMS's proposed rule for Medicare Advantage (Part C) and Prescription Drug Plans (Part D), aimed at ensuring protection of beneficiaries (especially older adults and dually eligible individuals).

rubrics_metrics.name: SHIP Program Awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposing removal of State Health Insurance Assistance Program references from marketing disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates should oppose CMS proposals that remove references to SHIP in marketing disclaimers; explain how SHIP references help beneficiaries find unbiased assistance and why removal would harm consumer awareness and access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrollment Pressure Protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting separation between educational and sales activities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue for maintaining strong protections that separate education/outreach from sales/marketing to prevent enrollment pressure; provide examples of harms when separation is blurred and recommend concrete safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining prohibitions on inaccurate, misleading, and superlative advertising language
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support retention of prohibitions against inaccurate or misleading statements and against use of superlative claims in marketing; illustrate with sample marketing copy or real-world instances showing consumer confusion or harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language Access
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserving notice requirements for interpretation services
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate that CMS keep notice requirements about availability of interpretation services and language assistance; explain how removing notices would impede non-English-speaking or limited-English-proficiency enrollees from accessing meaningful information.

rubrics_metrics.name: D-SNP Care Coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting enhanced coordination for dually eligible individuals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support policies that strengthen care coordination for D-SNPs (Dual-Eligible Special Needs Plans); provide reasoning and examples of care coordination needs for dually eligible beneficiaries and how enhancements would improve outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: State D-SNP Oversight
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support stronger state oversight of D-SNPs, including mechanisms for monitoring and enforcement; give examples of state oversight practices that protect beneficiaries and recommend specific oversight tools or reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: C-SNP/I-SNP Concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Addressing potential gaps in care coordination
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raise concerns about gaps in care coordination for Chronic Condition SNPs (C-SNPs) and Institutional SNPs (I-SNPs); explain specific coordination failures and propose regulatory fixes or clarifying language to ensure continuity of care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Benefits Notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposing removal of mid-year notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue against removing mid-year notice requirements related to supplemental benefits; describe why mid-year notices are important for beneficiary awareness and decisionmaking and provide examples of harms if notices were removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Authorization Transparency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support maintaining transparency requirements for prior authorization, including public reporting; explain how reporting promotes accountability and helps identify access barriers, and provide suggested metrics or reporting elements if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable Access Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposing deletions of specific protected group references
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppose CMS deletions of explicit references to protected groups in equitable access standards; explain why explicit references are necessary to ensure nondiscrimination and equitable access, and cite statutory or policy authority when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad RFI (Request for Information) Topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing feedback on integration, provider networks, accessibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to CMS's broad requests for information by offering evidence and examples on topics such as integration of services, adequacy of provider networks, and accessibility; suggest specific questions CMS should address and recommended data sources or metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Strategy: Use Specific Examples and Protect Privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should include specific examples, client stories, and organizational experiences while preserving enrollee privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting comments, include concrete examples and client narratives to show real-world impact but redact or anonymize identifying information to preserve enrollee privacy; explain organizational experience and include data where feasible to strengthen arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Template Comment Structure (Justice in Aging Approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each topic addressed, the template suggests a structured format for comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow this structure: (1) Start with the proposed change being addressed; (2) State support, opposition, or partial support; (3) Provide a brief justification (2-4 sentences); (4) Include 1-2 specific examples or client stories where possible; (5) Suggest specific regulatory language amendments; (6) Reference relevant statutory authority (e.g., Social Security Act sections). Using this structure ensures clarity, ties comments to legal authority, and makes actionable suggestions for regulatory text.
